newsitem.title: Philippines: Manila stocks end up for eight straight day.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end up for eight straight day.

text.p: Manila stocks, powered by buying on food-linked issues, rose for the eight consecutive session on Friday despite earlier projections of a technical correction, brokers said.
The main index hovered near its 3,100-point after it closed 26.94 points higher at 3,090.
The Philippine index has soared by 237.84 points since it started its uptrend on October 29.
Brisk trading Alaska Milk, poultry firm Vitarich Corp, ice cream maker Selecta and meat processor Swift sustained the market's rise, said Henry Ong, analyst at Sapphire Securities.
"Investors picked up food stocks, which were cheaply traded at 10 times PE (projected earnings in 1997), due to recovery prospects next year," Ong said.
Softening of major commodity inputs such as sugar, corn and milk will improve the financial picture of food firms, he said.
Brokers said they expect the market to pause for breath early next week after the main index hit the 3,100 level.
